instructions: Pat the 1 1/2 lb cod dry with paper towels and lay it in a baking dish in one layer.

Mix the 1 tsp cumin, 3/4 tsp of the salt, the 1/2 tsp black pepper and 1/2 tsp of the Aleppo pepper in a small bowl. Sprinkle it over both sides of the fish, drizzle on 2 tbsp of the olive oil and rub it all over.
Meanwhile, grate the 2 garlic cloves into a bowl. Add the 1/2 cup tahini, the juice of the lemon and the last 1/4 tsp salt, and stir with a fork. It'll go thick and stiff at first. That's normal.
Whisk in water 1 tbsp at a time, about 1/3 cup in all, until the sauce is smooth and runs easily off a spoon. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.

Take the fish out and spoon the tahini sauce over it until it's covered. Bake for another 5 to 8 minutes, until the sauce is hot at the edges and the fish flakes when you press the thickest part with a fork. If you have a thermometer, you're looking for 140°F in the thickest part.

While it bakes, heat the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil in a small skillet over medium low. Add the 1/4 cup pine nuts and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're golden. Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto a plate.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir the last 1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper and the 1/4 tsp cayenne into the warm oil. Pour it into a small bowl for the table.
Chop a small handful of the parsley. Scatter it and the pine nuts over the fish.
Serve with warm pita bread, with the chili oil on the side.
method_notes: All three bake cod at 400°F seasoned with salt and a hot pepper, cover it with a tahini, lemon and garlic sauce, and finish with toasted nuts and fresh herbs. Feel Good Foodie rubs the fish with cumin, black pepper and cayenne and whisks a raw tahini sauce to pour over once it's baked; Unicorns in the Kitchen and Hungry Paprikas cook onion, garlic and cilantro into a warm sauce, and Hungry Paprikas lets you swap in almonds or cashews for the pine nuts. This one follows Feel Good Foodie's spice rub and raw sauce, bakes the sauce on for the last few minutes, and moves most of the heat into a chili oil for the table. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Lebanese) has no version, so the first read version leads.
